big: Meena's bank freezes her account because her NRI paperwork is out of date. She is abroad, her mother needs money, and she cannot reach the account. A little paperwork each year would have avoided this.

lines: Why do banks ask so many forms of NRIs?
Because global rules like FATCA and CRS make banks report foreign tax residents. Keep your KYC current, and use a power of attorney only with care.

rows: Rules under which banks share details of foreign tax residents
Passport, visa and overseas address, to open accounts and invest
Lets a trusted person act for you, so keep it narrow
NRO funds can go abroad up to a yearly cap, with papers
note: Rules change, so check the current rule with your bank or a qualified adviser.

title: Compliance and paperwork
stops: Banks collect details under FATCA and CRS
A power of attorney should be as wide as possible
NRI KYC needs an overseas address
NRO funds can go abroad without any limit
caps: Rules require sharing of foreign tax residents' details.
Keep it limited to specific tasks, and drafted with care.
Passport, visa and overseas address are typical.
There is a yearly cap on NRO transfers, with conditions.

q: A bank asks Rohan for a self-declaration of his tax residency. What is the reason?
opts: A new bank holiday on the calendar
A local festival in the town
why: A mood has nothing to do with banking regulation.
These rules make banks collect foreign tax residency details.
A bank holiday has no link to the form being asked.
A festival has no link to a regulatory form.

q: Meena gives a relative a very wide power of attorney. What is the risk?
opts: Misuse of her accounts and assets
None, since relatives are always safe
why: A wide power can be used to act far beyond what she wanted.
Trust does not remove the risk of misuse.
A PAN does not lapse because of a power.
A bank does not close because of a power.

q: What is the usual cap on moving NRO funds abroad?
opts: No limit of any kind at all
A monthly cap of a single rupee
Only on bank holidays of the year
why: There is a limit, so this claim is wrong.
The limit is not a monthly cap of one rupee.
The cap is yearly, and it needs documents and conditions.
Holidays have no link to the limit on transfers.

q: Which habit avoids a frozen account?
opts: Never reply to any message from the bank
Change the name on the account often
Give a wrong address when asked
Keep KYC and overseas address current
why: Ignoring the bank leads to the account being frozen.
Changing the name often causes mismatch trouble.
A wrong address is a legal risk and gives trouble later.
Current KYC keeps the account active and compliant.

pts: FATCA and CRS make banks collect foreign tax residency details.
Keep NRI KYC current. Keep a power of attorney narrow.
NRO transfers abroad have a yearly limit and need papers.
